title: 6 Years of Electoral Bonds, Then 1 Verdict #Shorts
description:
Source: Supreme Court, ADR v. Union of India (2024). Should parties disclose every donor?
For about six years, electoral bonds let people fund political parties without the public knowing who gave. On 15 February 2024, a five-judge bench led by CJI D.Y. Chandrachud unanimously struck the scheme down, saying voters have a right to know who funds politics. A month later, the court refused SBI's request for months more and gave it until the next day.
Subscribe for the questions behind every story, explained in a minute.
Sources: Supreme Court judgment, ADR v. Union of India, 2024 INSC 113 (15 Feb 2024); Supreme Court order of 11 March 2024 (reported by The Tribune, Outlook/PTI).
This video is commentary. The anchors are AI-made.
#IndianPolitics #Sawaal #Accountability #ElectoralBonds #Shorts

script:
SLOT: Thu 29 Oct 2026, 15:00 IST (Short 2 of 2 today). English; Hindi dub auto-generated by the system 2 hours later. Evergreen explainer, not breaking news. Cast: Aditya and Nisha (channel-config looks/voices). No AI faces or voices of real people.

SCRIPT:
ADITYA (desk): "About six years. That's how long electoral bonds ran before the Supreme Court struck them down."
NISHA (VO): "Sawaal Explainer. Brought in via the 2017 Finance Bill, launched 2018. On petitions including ADR's and CPI(M)'s, a five-judge bench led by CJI Chandrachud struck it down unanimously on 15 February 2024."
ADITYA (VO): "The main ground: voters' right to information under Article 19(1)(a). Funding information, the bench said, is essential to vote effectively. Linked changes to three laws also fell."
NISHA (desk): "The government argued the scheme protected donor privacy and moved donations away from cash. The court rejected that."
ADITYA (VO): "What many missed: SBI asked for time until 30 June. On 11 March, the court refused, gave SBI until the next day, and warned it could act for wilful disobedience."
NISHA (VO): "Commentary. Our questions: the challenge was filed in 2017, so why did the scheme keep running? Why did SBI want months for data the court had asked for within weeks?"
ADITYA (desk): "And will the government now back full donor transparency?"
NISHA (desk): "Should parties disclose every donor: yes or no? Follow Sawaal for the question behind every story."
